- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to correct; add a 1–2 day lag correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate in high-sentiment periods; apply a +0.5–1.0% bias adjustment if sentiment > 0.33 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), model is prone to overfitting to recent noise; use 3–5 day moving average for smoothing.
